Performance at a glance

The leaderboard depends on how you rank — and under what conditions

One aggregation knob re-ranks the same frozen backbones; four condition knobs redefine the score matrix underneath. The Kendall τ-b panel measures how much the order reshuffles when a single condition flips. All rankings are precomputed offline with evaluma.

The four condition knobs each swap the underlying score matrix rather than just filtering it. Probe chooses how frozen embeddings become predictions — a linear probe or KNN-5. Bands sets which channels the backbone sees — RGB only, or the full multispectral stack. Pooling sets how patch features collapse to one vector — spatial patch-mean, or the transformer CLS token (available only for transformer backbones, so those slices rank fewer models). Flipping any knob re-scores every model and can reorder the board or drop models with incomplete coverage into the Excluded panel.

worst → best (per dataset) bold = column best # rank under the selected aggregation n datasets evaluated (coverage) cells: top-1 accuracy, or micro-mAP for BigEarthNet

Rank dispersion

Aggregate rank on the x-axis, per-dataset rank spread on the y-axis.

Left = stronger aggregate rank. Lower = more consistent dataset-by-dataset ranking.

Pin a model to keep its dispersion profile visible while you compare conditions.

Rank sensitivity (Kendall τ-b)?

How much the ranking survives flipping one condition, holding the other three at your current settings. τ-b runs +1 (identical order) to −1 (reversed); near 1 = stable.
